question: Bhirrana, a Neolithic site, is situated in __________state. (RPF SI CBT-I 2024 (02/12/2024) Shift 1)
options: Rajasthan
Madhya Pradesh
Gujarat
Haryana
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Haryana

Explanation:
Bhirrana is an important Neolithic site located in the Fatehabad district of Haryana. Situated on the banks of the Saraswati River, this site has yielded remains that predate the Harappan civilization. Excavations at Bhirrana have uncovered pottery and stone tools, indicating the region's ancient settlement. The site provides crucial insights into the early phase of the Indus Valley Civilization. Other significant Neolithic sites in Haryana include Rakhigarhi and Banawali.

question_hi: नवपाषाण कालीन स्थल भिरराणा किस राज्य में स्थित है? (RPF SI CBT-I 2024 (02/12/2024) Shift 1)

Explanation:

question: Which official in the Gupta administration was responsible for peace and war matters? (RRB JE ECE (22/04/2025) Shift 1 CBT 2)
options: Vishayapati
Sandhi-Vigrahika
Mahapratihara
Mahadandanayaka
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Sandhi-Vigrahika

Explanation:
In the Gupta administration, Sandhi-Vigrahika was the official responsible for peace (sandhi) and war (vigraha) matters. This position is comparable to a modern minister of external affairs or defense. Vishayapati was the administrative head of a district or province, handling revenue collection and local order. Mahapratihara served as the chief gatekeeper or security officer of the royal palace. Mahadandanayaka was the commander of the army or a judicial officer, dealing with military and legal affairs. The Gupta administration had a well-organized hierarchy of officials, reflecting efficient governance. Understanding these roles is important for exams covering ancient Indian polity.

☛ Who was the chief security officer of the Gupta royal palace? → Mahapratihara

question_hi: गुप्त प्रशासन में कौन-सा अधिकारी शांति और युद्ध के मामलों के लिए जिम्मेदार था? (RRB JE ECE (22/04/2025) Shift 1 CBT 2)
options_hi: विषयपति
संधि-विग्रहीक
महाप्रतिहार
महादंडनायक
solution_hi:
Solution: सही उत्तर है संधि-विग्रहीक

Explanation:
गुप्त प्रशासन में संधि-विग्रहीक शांति (संधि) और युद्ध (विग्रह) के मामलों के लिए जिम्मेदार एक महत्वपूर्ण अधिकारी था। यह पद आधुनिक विदेश मंत्री या रक्षा मंत्री के समान माना जाता है। विषयपति एक जिले या प्रांत का प्रशासनिक प्रमुख होता था, जो राजस्व संग्रह और स्थानीय व्यवस्था देखता था। महाप्रतिहार महल के द्वारपाल या मुख्य सुरक्षा अधिकारी के रूप में कार्य करता था, जो राजा की सुरक्षा में तैनात रहता था। महादंडनायक सेना का प्रमुख या न्यायिक अधिकारी होता था, जिसका कार्य सैन्य और न्यायिक दोनों क्षेत्रों में था। गुप्त काल में इस प्रकार के पदों का सुव्यवस्थित ढाँचा था, जो शासन की कुशलता को दर्शाता है।

question: The maximum number of Buddhist stupas had been built by which of the following rulers? (RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (17/06/2025) Shift 3)
options: Ashoka
Pushyamitra Sunga
Chandragupta Maurya
Bimbisara
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Ashoka

Explanation:
Ashoka (268-232 BCE), the third emperor of the Maurya dynasty, embraced Buddhism after the Kalinga War. He commissioned the construction of a large number of Buddhist stupas and pillars across India and regions like Nepal, Sri Lanka, and Afghanistan. Texts like 'Divyavadana' and 'Ashokavadana' mention that Ashoka built 84,000 stupas. Famous stupas like Sanchi Stupa and Bharhut Stupa belong to his period. Pushyamitra Sunga was anti-Buddhist, Chandragupta Maurya was a Jain, and Bimbisara followed Buddhism but built fewer stupas than Ashoka. Thus, Ashoka built the maximum number of stupas.

☛ Ashoka's Buddhist teacher → Upagupta
☛ Language of Ashoka's edicts → Prakrit
☛ Location of Sanchi Stupa → Madhya Pradesh
☛ Famous stupa built by Ashoka → Sanchi Stupa
question_hi: निम्नलिखित में से किस शासक द्वारा अधिकतम संख्या में बौद्ध स्तूपों का निर्माण कराया गया था? (RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (17/06/2025) Shift 3)
options_hi: अशोक
पुष्यमित्र शुंग
चंद्रगुप्त मौर्य
बिम्बिसार
solution_hi:
Solution: सही उत्तर है अशोक

Explanation:
मौर्य साम्राज्य के तीसरे सम्राट अशोक (268-232 ई.पू.) ने कलिंग युद्ध के बाद बौद्ध धर्म अपना लिया था। उन्होंने पूरे भारत तथा नेपाल, श्रीलंका, अफगानिस्तान जैसे क्षेत्रों में बड़ी संख्या में बौद्ध स्तूप और स्तंभों का निर्माण कराया। 'दिव्यावदान' और 'अशोकावदान' ग्रंथों में उल्लेख है कि अशोक ने 84,000 स्तूप बनवाए। प्रसिद्ध सांची का स्तूप और भरहुत का स्तूप उन्हीं के काल के हैं। पुष्यमित्र शुंग बौद्ध विरोधी थे, चंद्रगुप्त मौर्य जैन थे, और बिम्बिसार बौद्ध धर्म के अनुयायी थे किंतु उनके द्वारा स्तूप निर्माण का इतिहास अशोक से कम है। अतः अशोक ने सर्वाधिक स्तूप निर्माण कराए।

question: Who defeated Harshavardhana on the Narmada frontier? (RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (21/06/2025) Shift 3)
options: Rajaraja Chola
Narasimhavarman
Pulakesin II
Mahendravarman II
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Pulakesin II

Explanation:
Harshavardhana (606-647 AD) was a powerful emperor who ruled over a large part of North India. He attempted to expand his empire southward but was defeated by the Chalukya king Pulakesin II (610-642 AD) on the banks of the Narmada river. This battle took place around 618-619 AD. After this defeat, Harsha did not attempt to expand further south, and the Narmada river became the boundary between the two empires. Pulakesin II was one of the greatest rulers of the Chalukya dynasty, ruling from their capital Vatapi (present-day Badami). His victory over Harsha is mentioned in the Aihole inscription, which praises his military achievements. This event highlights the strength of the Chalukya kingdom in the Deccan region during the early medieval period.

question_hi: नर्मदा सीमा पर हर्षवर्धन को किसने पराजित किया था? (RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (21/06/2025) Shift 3)
options_hi: राजराज चोल
नरसिंहवर्मन
पुलाकेशिन द्वितीय
महेन्द्रवर्मन द्वितीय
solution_hi:
Solution: सही उत्तर है पुलाकेशिन द्वितीय

Explanation:
हर्षवर्धन (606-647 ई.) एक प्रतापी सम्राट थे जिन्होंने उत्तर भारत के बड़े हिस्से पर शासन किया। उन्होंने अपने साम्राज्य का दक्षिण की ओर विस्तार करने का प्रयास किया, लेकिन नर्मदा नदी के तट पर चालुक्य राजा पुलाकेशिन द्वितीय (610-642 ई.) से उनका सामना हुआ। पुलाकेशिन द्वितीय ने हर्षवर्धन को पराजित किया, जिससे भारत के दक्षिणी भाग पर चालुक्यों का प्रभुत्व बना रहा। यह युद्ध लगभग 618-619 ई. में हुआ था। इस हार के बाद हर्षवर्धन ने दक्षिण की ओर विस्तार का प्रयास नहीं किया और नर्मदा नदी दोनों साम्राज्यों की सीमा बन गई। पुलाकेशिन द्वितीय चालुक्य वंश के सबसे महान शासकों में से एक थे और उन्होंने वातापी (बादामी) से शासन किया।

question: The royal title used by Chandragupta I was: (RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (18/06/2025) Shift 3)
options: Maharaj
Chakravartin
Samrat
Maharajadhiraja
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Maharajadhiraja

Explanation:
Chandragupta I was a ruler of the Gupta dynasty who reigned around 320 CE. He adopted the title 'Maharajadhiraja', meaning 'Great King of Kings', which signified supreme imperial authority. This title was used during the Gupta period to denote the highest sovereign power. Chandragupta I strengthened his position by marrying the Lichchhavi princess Kumaradevi. His coins also bear this title. Other options like 'Maharaj' and 'Samrat' were of lower status, while 'Chakravartin' was used later. Thus, the royal title of Chandragupta I was Maharajadhiraja.

question_hi: चंद्रगुप्त प्रथम द्वारा उपयोग की जानेवाली शाही उपाधि _________थी।  (RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (18/06/2025) Shift 3)
options_hi: महाराज
चक्रवर्ती
सम्राट
महाराजाधिराज
solution_hi:
Solution: सही उत्तर है महाराजाधिराज

Explanation:
चंद्रगुप्त प्रथम गुप्त वंश का शासक था जिसने 320 ई. के आसपास शासन किया। उसने 'महाराजाधिराज' की उपाधि धारण की, जिसका अर्थ 'राजाओं का महान राजा' है। यह उपाधि उच्चतम साम्राज्यिक दर्शाती थी। गुप्त काल में इस उपाधि का प्रयोग सर्वोच्च शक्ति को इंगित करने के लिए किया जाता था। चंद्रगुप्त प्रथम ने लिच्छवि राजकुमारी कुमारदेवी से विवाह कर अपनी स्थिति मजबूत की। उसके सिक्कों पर भी यह उपाधि अंकित है। अन्य विकल्प जैसे 'महाराज' और 'सम्राट' निम्न स्तर के थे, जबकि 'चक्रवर्ती' का प्रयोग बाद में किया गया। इस प्रकार, चंद्रगुप्त प्रथम की शाही उपाधि 'महाराजाधिराज' थी।

question: What does 'Dhamma' primarily refer to in Ashoka’s inscriptions? (RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (18/06/2025) Shift 3)
options: Slogans of Buddha
Royal decree
Buddhist doctrine
Moral law
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Moral law

Explanation:
In Ashoka's inscriptions, the term 'Dhamma' primarily refers to Moral law or a code of conduct. It focused on practical ethical principles for the common people, rather than the deeper philosophical aspects of Buddhism. Ashoka promoted 'Dhamma' through principles like non-violence, truth, compassion, and social harmony. He expected his subjects to respect parents, teachers, and elders, practice charity, and be kind to all living beings. The aim of 'Dhamma' was to establish unity and peace among different religions and communities. It was not a specific religious doctrine but a universal moral code that Ashoka considered essential for governance and social order. The 'Dhamma' was propagated through edicts inscribed on pillars and rocks, and special officers known as Dhamma Mahamatras were appointed to spread its message.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:
☛ What was 'Dhamma' based on in Ashoka's inscriptions? → Moral law and social conduct
☛ Which officer did Ashoka appoint to propagate his 'Dhamma'? → Dhamma Mahamatra
☛ What was the significance of non-violence in Ashoka's 'Dhamma'? → Renouncing war, violence, and animal sacrifice
☛ Which of Ashoka's edicts clearly explains 'Dhamma'? → 13th Major Rock Edict
☛ How is Ashoka's 'Dhamma' different from Buddhism? → Emphasizes social ethics rather than spiritual liberation

question: The Indo-Greek king who issued coins with bilingual inscriptions was: (RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (19/06/2025) Shift 2)

question: The Jain monastic establishments are called as: (RRB NTPC CBT-I (23/02/2021) Shift 1)

question: Who handled judicial matters in the provinces during the reign of the Gupta Empire? (RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (23/06/2025) Shift 2)

Ayuktaka

question: What is the primary function of ‘viharas’ in Buddhist architecture? (RRB JE CBT-I 2024 (16/12/2024) Shift 2)
options: To serve as meditation halls
To house relics
To serve as residential places for Buddhist priests
To hold public gatherings
solution:

Explanation:
In Buddhist architecture, viharas primarily functioned as residential places for Buddhist monks. These were monasteries where monks lived, studied, and meditated. Viharas were often located near stupas and chaityas. Early viharas were made of wood, but later cave viharas (e.g., Ajanta and Ellora) became common. They typically included cells for monks, prayer halls, and courtyards. Serving as meditation halls was the primary function of chaityas, while stupas housed relics. Thus, the main purpose of viharas was to provide accommodation for the monastic community.

question: What was the main purpose of the citadel in Harappan cities?  (RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (19/06/2025) Shift 1)

question: Which era is called golden age of ancient India? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (17/02/2021) Shift 1)
options: The Chola  Empire, 3rd century
The Mauryan Empire, 3rd century
The Gupta Empire, 4th century
The Kushan Empire, 1st century
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is The Gupta Empire, 4th century

Explanation:
The Gupta Empire (c. 320-550 CE) is known as the 'Golden Age' of ancient India. This period witnessed remarkable progress in literature, art, science, mathematics and philosophy. Chandragupta I established the Gupta dynasty in 320 CE, and Samudragupta expanded the empire. Under Chandragupta Vikramaditya, the empire reached its zenith. Renowned figures like Kalidasa (literature), Aryabhata (mathematics), and the establishment of Nalanda University belong to this era. Texts like Bhagavata Purana and Amarakosha were also composed during this period. Thus, the Gupta Empire is called the 'Golden Age' of ancient India.

question: Who deciphered a Brahmi inscription referring king Ashoka as Devanampiya Piyadasi? (RRB NTPC GRADUATE CBT 1 (19/03/2026) Shift 3)

Susan Bayly
James Princep

Explanation:
James Princep deciphered the Brahmi script in 1837 CE, proving that King Ashoka was referred to as 'Devanampiya Piyadasi' in the inscriptions. Brahmi was one of the major scripts of ancient India, used in Ashoka's edicts. Princep studied the Hathigumpha inscription of Kalinga and various coins to crack the script. Deciphering Brahmi was a historic achievement, connecting the Mauryan period with later Indian history. Princep also collaborated with scholars like Thomas Daniell and William Jones.

question: Which of the following administrative features was a key characteristic of the Mauryan Empire under Chandragupta Maurya? (RRB NTPC GRADUATE CBT 1 (19/03/2026) Shift 3)
options: Feudal land grant system
Hereditary provincial governors
Centralised bureaucracy guided by Arthashastra
Revenue collection by religious institutions
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Centralised bureaucracy guided by Arthashastra

Explanation:
Under Chandragupta Maurya, the defining administrative feature of the Mauryan Empire was a centralised bureaucracy guided by the Arthashastra (written by Kautilya). This system had the king as supreme, with provinces administered by governors who were not hereditary. The empire was divided into provinces, districts, and villages, with a detailed hierarchy of officials overseeing tax collection, law and order, irrigation, and trade. The Arthashastra provided the framework for administration, economy, and military strategy, ensuring efficient governance. Unlike feudal or religious systems, this state-controlled bureaucracy was highly structured and documented.
